sources.news_title: Upstate N.Y. child dies after contracting measles, a first in 30 years
sources.text:
A child in upstate New York's North Country has become the state's first known measles-associated death in more than 30 years, the state Department of Health and Lewis County Public Health said in a joint statement Monday.
"We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child's family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time,” the departments said. “Measles is a highly contagious disease that can cause serious complications and death.
Officials suggest parents have their children vaccinated against measles, especially if you are traveling to any high-risk areas.
"We urge New Yorkers to ensure they are up to date on measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccinations and speak to their healthcare provider about immunizations,” the departments said.
State health officials on Monday said that as of Oct. 24, there have been 178 total measles cases in New York, all but eight of them upstate.
On Oct. 5, Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state disaster emergency over the growing numbers of measles cases statewide, particularly in rural areas and in neighboring states.
“I am heartbroken to learn that a child in Lewis County has died after contracting measles,” Hochul said in a statement. “As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through. My heart goes out to everyone who knew and loved this child.”
In September, the state launched a new measles database that updates each Tuesday, breaking cases down by county.

sources.news_title: New York Reports First Measles Death in Over 30 Years Amid US Outbreak
sources.text:
New York state reports first measles-linked child death in over 30 years amid outbreak
- Published OnNov 3, 2026 | 07:28 IST
- Last Updated OnNov 3, 2026 | 07:28 IST
State health officials are ramping up outreach and localized vaccination drives as the nation faces its worst measles resurgence in decades, driven by a policy shift in federal mortality tracking. Discover how regional health agencies plan to address surging infection clusters in neighboring counties.
The New York State Department of Health said on Monday that a child in Lewis County had died in connection with an ongoing measles outbreak, marking the state's first known measles-associated death in more than 30 years.
In October, Governor Kathy Hochul declared a State Disaster Emergency in response to the measles outbreak across areas of New York and neighboring states.
"The Department has offered resources to Lewis County to assist with community outreach and support local vaccination efforts – both in response to this case, and as part of our ongoing efforts to support counties that are facing this ongoing measles outbreak," the state department said.
The death comes as the US experiences its worst measles resurgence in decades.
Hochul told Reuters in October that the state would seek federal assistance to help contain the outbreak, but did not confirm whether it had submitted a formal request for a Centers for Disease Control and Prevention Epidemic Intelligence Service, or Epi-Aid, response.
As of October 24, New York had reported 178 measles cases this year, including 170 cases outside New York City and 8 cases in New York City.
State health officials said they were working with county health departments and local partners to provide measles, mumps and rubella vaccinations to unvaccinated individuals who request them and to investigate reported cases.
The US Department of Health and Human Services did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment outside business hours.
The CDC has recorded three measles-related deaths this year, but did not name the states where they occurred.
Pennsylvania has been the epicenter of the outbreak this year, reporting 1,433 confirmed cases and five measles-associated deaths so far this year.
The gap in numbers follows a policy shift under US Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., with the CDC switching to the National Center for Health Statistics' mortality data to track measles deaths, replacing its earlier reliance on state health departments' figures.

sources.news_title: Child dies of measles upstate in first New York death related to disease in 30 years
sources.text:
Child dies of measles upstate in first New York death related to disease in 30 years
For the first time in 30 years, a child in New York has died after contracting measles, state health officials said late Monday.
The child was in upstate Lewis County but officials did not release an age or whether the child had received the measles vaccine. Officials described it as the state’s first known measles related death in three decades.
Measles cases have surged throughout the United States in recent years, mostly due to communities that are unvaccinated or undervaccinated, experts have said.
There have been 178 measles cases in the state as of Oct. 24, 170 in New York State outside of the city, and eight in New York City, officials said. Lewis County accounts for 15 of those cases.
In 2025, there were 48 cases statewide and 15 in 2024.
On Long Island, a young unvaccinated child in Nassau County tested positive for measles earlier this year and last month an unvaccinated man over the age of 50 tested positive after visiting several medical offices across the county.
Last month, Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a state disaster emergency due to the steady increase in cases, especially in rural counties.
In a statement released Monday night, Hochul said she was “heartbroken” to learn about the child’s death.
“We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak,” the state Health Department and Lewis County Health Department said in a joint statement. “We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child’s family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time.”
They reminded New Yorkers that measles is a highly contagious respiratory virus that can lead to serious illness and death, encouraging them to make sure they and their family members are up to date with their measles vaccination.
“The Department has offered resources to Lewis County to assist with community outreach and support local vaccination efforts — both in response to this case, and as part of our ongoing efforts to support counties that are facing this ongoing measles outbreak,” the statement said.
Symptoms of measles include high fever, cough, runny nose and red watery eyes as well as a rash across the body.

Child in New York dies after contracting measles, governor says
By Katherine Dillinger, CNN
(CNN) — A child in Lewis County, New York, has died after contracting measles, Gov. Kathy Hochul said in a statement Monday. It is the state’s first measles-related death in 30 years.
“As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through. My heart goes out to everyone who knew and loved this child,” she said. “Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination remains our best protection against this dangerous disease. This is New York’s first measles-related death in 30 years, a devastating reminder of what’s at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.
“In New York, we will continue to stand by proven public health measures and do everything we can to keep New Yorkers safe and healthy.”
CNN has reached out to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the New York state health department and the Lewis County health department for more information.
Surging measles cases prompted Hochul to declare a statewide disaster emergency last month. As of Thursday, 168 cases had been reported across New York, according to data from the CDC. Lewis County reported 15 cases as of October 14, all in people who had not received the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine.
Measles typically causes about 1 in 5 people who aren’t vaccinated to be hospitalized, according to the CDC. As many as 1 out of every 20 children with measles gets pneumonia, the most common cause of death from measles in young children. One of every 1,000 kids with measles will develop encephalitis, or brain swelling.
More than 4,800 measles cases have been reported across the US this year, according to the CDC – the most since 1991, almost a decade before measles was declared eliminated in the US. More than a quarter of those cases have been in Pennsylvania, which has reported five measles-related deaths.
The Pan American Health Organization, an arm of the World Health Organization, is set to hold a measles elimination commission meeting next week, when the US is widely expected to lose the elimination status it has held since 2000.
Public health experts have largely attributed the rise in measles cases in the US to falling vaccination rates, although rising cases have driven a surge of immunizations in some places.
Two doses of the MMR vaccine are recommended in childhood to provide 97% protection against measles infections.
In 2024, 93% of US 3-year-olds had received at least one MMR dose, according to data from the CDC’s National Immunization Surveys, below the 95% threshold needed to prevent outbreaks of the highly contagious disease. But in 2025 — a year marked by the nation’s first measles deaths in decades — the level rose to 97% among 3-year-olds.
US Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. has drawn broad criticism for his response to measles outbreaks, including downplaying the immunity provided by the MMR vaccine. In Pennsylvania, the measles-related deaths have also sparked a war of words between Kennedy and state officials.
President Donald Trump has also repeated misinformation about vaccines, including linking them with autism and saying that children have “a tremendous amount of vaccines” put in their bodies.
CNN’s Deidre McPhillips and Meg Tirrell contributed to this report.

sources.text:
New York health officials Monday reported the state’s first measles-associated death in more than 30 years.
A child in a rural county in northern New York died.
“We are deeply saddened by the death of a child in Lewis County associated with the ongoing measles outbreak. We extend our heartfelt condolences to the child’s family and loved ones and ask that their privacy be respected during this difficult time,” state health officials said in a statement.
The statement did not provide additional details about the child.
So far this year, 178 measles cases have been recorded in New York, according to the state Health Department. The vast majority — 170 cases — were outside New York City. Fifteen cases have been reported in Lewis County.
In October, Gov. Kathy Hochul declared the outbreak an emergency.
“Measles is highly contagious, and vaccination remains our best protection against this dangerous disease,” she said in a statement after the death was announced Monday.
In neighboring Pennsylvania, health officials are fighting the country’s worst outbreak in 30 years. As of Monday, there have been 1,433 cases, according to the Pennsylvania Health Department, including 269 hospitalizations. Six people have died.
